critic.contradictions:
I re-checked six cross-lens conflicts myself. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DSSE/85db304a-b0fa-5d03-b685-f9acf8fac842/scratchpad/analysis/critic/: run c00_load.py first, then c01 to c06.

(1) Is the ICL dataset-level null informative, and is shot selection a big variance source?
- The claims: statistics says reliability is about 0 and the null was "unmeasurable". Measurement says reliability is about 0.45 and that "which 16 rows are shown is a large source of variance". Triggers says shots have no effect once the outlier is removed.
- My test (c01.py) uses two exact permutation nulls. Within-dataset (seed-to-seed) variance of run wrong rates is 3.12x the null with all 96 runs (p<0.001), but 0.81x (p=0.86) without icl__dsse1-08152__k16__s0. Between-dataset variance of the 3-seed means is 1.84x the null without that run (p=0.002). The implied true dataset SD is 0.015, against about 0.17 for FT.
- Verdict: triggers is right. All "shot variance" and the near-zero ICC come from one run. The statistics lens's "reliability about 0" applies only to variance-based ICC with that run included. Rank reliability, which is what the Spearman correlations depend on, is about 0.45 even with it and about 0.58 without it.
- So the null is weakly informative. It rules out a true icl~ft correlation of about 0.5 or more, but not one of about 0.3. For icl~14B it only rules out about 0.7 or more.

(2) Does ICL shift answer form dataset-specifically toward FT?
- The claims: statistics says yes (math words rho 0.56, in-domain 0.62-0.75, "format is not purely a weight effect"). Measurement says no reliable movement.
- My test (c02.py), n=31, outlier excluded:
  - icl~ft log words: 0.52 [0.11, 0.79].
  - Same, controlling for the dataset's training-row length: 0.31 [-0.14, 0.66].
  - In-domain words icl~ft: 0.62, falling to 0.06 with row length controlled (n=30).
  - FT tracks row length at 0.86 (math) and 0.95 (in-domain); ICL at 0.44 and 0.64.
- Verdict: the "proportional" link is a common cause. Both routes imitate the length of the dataset's rows. It is not ICL reproducing the FT mechanism, so measurement is closer to right.
- Statistics is right that ICL shortens answers in the same direction (by about 18% overall). But c06.py shows that 62-89% of the categorical style change from base to k=32 (boxed answers, "We are given", openings with "Let's") is already present at k=1. Only 10% of the length change is. That pattern fits a generic multi-turn effect, which was never controlled for.

(3) Are math damage and brevity "one mechanism" (error_anatomy) or is the damage "mostly not mediated by brevity" (competence)?
- My test (c03.py), FT n=3,100 answers, 0 truncated:
  - Share of answers without arithmetic: 0.51 (loose definition) or 0.27 (strict).
  - Effect of no arithmetic on being wrong, within problem and dataset: +0.12 [0.08, 0.17] (loose) and +0.16 [0.10, 0.23] (strict).
  - That mediates only 11-17% of the +0.38 excess error over the ICL reference.
  - Answers that do show arithmetic carry 34-59% of the excess, and their wrong rate still tracks 14B at rho 0.42 (n=31).
  - At dataset level, no-arithmetic share and wrong rate correlate 0.92.
- Verdict: both are right, at different levels. Across datasets there is one strength factor. At the answer level, most of the damage is not explained by visibly skipped working (and this answer-level estimate is post-treatment, not causal). error_anatomy's reading "the answer is fixed in the first tokens" overreaches.

(4) Is the jackpot run's failure pattern FT-like?
- The claims: the statistics verifier says yes; the triggers verifier says it is no more FT-like than base (rho 0.52 vs 0.50).
- My test (c04.py): the jackpot's per-problem wrongness correlates 0.53 with the FT profile, the highest of all 96 runs (the others range 0.33-0.51). Controlling for the leave-one-out ICL difficulty profile, the partial correlation is 0.39. The other 95 ICL runs range from -0.19 to 0.16; the FT runs have median 0.48 (range 0.07-0.60).
- Verdict: the statistics verifier is right. The triggers metric did not remove difficulty shared by all routes.
- It is still not the complete FT phenotype: it keeps markdown bold in 72% of answers (FT 0.1%), and FT on its own dataset is mild (wrong 0.41).

(5) Does brevity carry transfer information beyond the error rate?
- The claims: measurement says both carry independent signal (DSSE n=92). dsse_crosscheck says this is fragile.
- My test (c05.py), n=92, partial Spearman of w40 with 14B:
  - controlling Opus error: 0.34 [0.10, 0.51]
  - controlling Gemma error: 0.15 [-0.08, 0.35]
  - controlling both: 0.14 [-0.12, 0.36]
  - For 8B it survives (0.27-0.28).
  - The reverse holds under every check: error beyond brevity is 0.31 for 14B, 0.47 for 8B and 0.58 for 4B.
- Verdict: dsse_crosscheck is right for 14B. Error beyond brevity is the robust half; brevity beyond error depends on the judge.

(6) Does early commitment track transfer?
- The measurement lens reports -0.07. Its verifier finds +0.3 to +0.5 after length adjustment. The dsse verifier finds +0.36 adjusted, but about 0 once the error rate is controlled.
- Reconciliation: the raw null is a length-suppression artifact (the measure needs at least 20 words after the answer). Early commitment rises with transfer only through the error rate, so it is not a separate carrier.

Smaller corrections:
- "Errors lag the register switch" (dynamics) is overstated. Counting truncations and no-number answers as failures, the step-4 accuracy loss is +0.14 to +0.33, significant in all 4 datasets, and about half complete.
- "ICL errors are base redraws" holds on average. But on 6 of 20 base-wrong problems, base's wrong value never appears among ICL's wrong answers (1.9 expected, p of about 0.005).
- "No other run has brevity shots" is false: six contexts have exactly one length request each, and none of them collapses.
critic.open_questions:
1. Neutral-context control. Would an unrelated multi-turn chat of the same token length (k=16-32) produce the same style shift: boxed 0.74 to 0.12, "We are given" 0.30 to 0.00, 150 to 121 words? 62-89% of the categorical change already happens at k=1. Without this control, "the context of these datasets changes form" cannot be told apart from "any chat history changes form".

2. Many-shot dose. ICL was tested only up to k=32 (2.7k tokens), while FT saw about 150 rows x 2 epochs plus gradients. Full-dataset ICL (k of about 150, 6-13k tokens) is feasible and untested. Without it, "context barely moves math" is a statement about k≤32 only.

3. Causal test of the jackpot. Steps: resample the identical 08152 seed-0 context with new seeds; ablate or reorder its 6 brevity-request rows; inject brevity-request rows into other datasets' contexts. Count, recency (3 of the last 4), phrasing ("no need for details": 3 of 3 such rows sit in s0) and question-length dependence are all confounded at n=1. The rate (1/96, CI 0.0003-0.057) is essentially unknown.

4. What transfers to 14B. Nobody has looked at the 14B answers. We do not know whether 14B becomes terse (the style transfers) or only wrong (the math transfers). We also do not know whether the Gemma judge marks non-committal terse answers as incorrect there. This decides whether "brevity tracks transfer" is a mechanism or a judge construct (point 5 of the contradictions).

5. Judging our own outputs. Our base, ICL and FT answers have no Opus or Gemma labels. Every route comparison rests on last-number or heuristic extractors, which inflate base and ICL by about 4pp.

6. Independent replicates. torch.manual_seed(0) is shared across runs: 3 of 4 ftcurve step-0 runs are byte-identical to base, and 17.5% of ICL answers are duplicated verbatim in another run. Base therefore has only 2 independent samples, and the ICL-minus-base difference (+0.03 [-0.03, +0.10]) leaves room for up to about 35% of ICL errors to be context-made.

7. Missing data, still unverified.
   - The missing ftcurve checkpoints are the length minima (estimated at about 9-12 words). They probably hide an error peak. 08377 has nothing between step 4 and step 76.
   - ft__dsse1-09037, the tersest top run, lacks response-level data; it was only imputed.
   - Both gaps make the FT-terseness contrasts conservative, and the shape of the learning curves untrustworthy.

8. ICL beyond the extreme groups. ICL exists only for the 32 extreme datasets, so no ICL correlation can be read as a population effect.

9. Learning-rate dependence. The "4 steps beat 32 shots by about 10x" result was obtained at peak learning rate 5e-4. No lower-learning-rate or exact-same-rows comparison exists.

10. Unexplained answer-level patterns.
    - Why FT answers that still show arithmetic are wrong 0.52 of the time (ICL: 0.23; on 2-step problems 0.32 vs base 0.04).
    - The roughly 40% of FT errors classified as "other".

sparks.claim: Fine-tuning produces a different kind of math error than context does. FT wrong answers are often 'shallow': a number copied from the question, or one operation on two question numbers. They are diffuse across runs and land far from gold. ICL wrong answers mostly re-draw the base model's own near-miss errors on the same hard problems. Context does not install the FT error mode; it leaves base's way of failing in place.
sparks.decisive_number: Within-problem matched excess of shallow errors, FT minus ICL: +0.137 [0.079, 0.194] (78 problems, problem bootstrap, Holm-significant). On unambiguously extracted answers: +0.185 [0.085, 0.283]. Agreement between wrong values at equal run counts: ICL 0.395 vs FT 0.164, difference +0.23 [0.14, 0.32]. On base-wrong problems, ICL wrong answers match base's wrong value 0.43 of the time, against an FT/ICL cross-match of 0.17. Replicated on DSSE's 92 fine-tuned models (n=5,500 wrong answers): shallow excess +0.194 [0.148, 0.242].
sparks.robustness: Holds_weaker after independent re-implementation. It survives problem-level and two-way bootstraps, a magnitude-matched null and a literal-numbers-only definition, and it gets larger on unambiguous extractions. Weak parts: the 'late-chain / penultimate step' half of the story (p=0.075 after Holm, concentrated on problem 5), and the literal 'about half are shallow', which is about 0.26 chance plus some extraction artifacts. It sits mostly in short FT answers: FT answers over 40 words differ from ICL only by +0.07.

sparks.claim: Context can reach the FT format-to-error phenotype, but very rarely. One of 96 random 16-row contexts (dsse1-08152 seed 0) switched Qwen3-1.7B into terse, working-free, FT-level-wrong answers. Its failure profile is FT-specific. The switch is all-or-nothing, not a graded tail, and it coincides with the only context holding a cluster of explicit brevity requests. Unrequested terse assistant turns alone never trigger it.
sparks.decisive_number: Wrong 0.66 vs 0.25/0.22 for its sister seeds, 0.24 for base and at most 0.35 for any of the other 95 runs (z=+13). 73% of its answers have at most 40 words; the maximum among the other 115 ICL runs is 4%. The gold number appears anywhere in only 36% of answers. My partial correlation of its per-problem wrongness with the FT profile, controlling for ICL difficulty, is 0.39; the other 95 ICL runs range from -0.19 to 0.16 and FT runs have median 0.48 (c04.py). It has 6/16 explicit brevity-request rows, unique among 116 contexts; 47 contexts whose rows all have at most 2 sentences never exceed 0.04 short answers.
sparks.robustness: The event is robust. It is not an extraction, truncation, batch or RNG artifact: 31 other seed-0 runs share the RNG stream, and an independent in-domain generation from the same context is also extreme (52 vs ≥147 words). The mechanism is n=1, with count, recency and phrasing confounded. It is not the complete FT phenotype: it keeps markdown bold in 72% of answers (FT 0.1%), and its terse mode depends on question length in a way FT's does not. Its rate is 1/96 (CI 0.0003-0.057).

sparks.claim: On the weight path the 'format effect' has two separable parts. (a) A fast, generic register switch, from markdown/LaTeX CoT to plain prose. It happens in top and bottom datasets alike and is roughly accuracy-neutral while arithmetic is still shown. (b) A dataset-specific brevity component, where the working is dropped. Only (b) tracks 14B transfer. FT also carries format from the advice domain to math much more strongly than context does. Context's own dataset-specific length signal is mostly just copying the dataset's row length.
sparks.decisive_number: After 4 LoRA steps (16 rows), markdown falls from 99% to 2-14% in all 4 curve datasets (0.86-0.98 of the total change). ICL at k=32 keeps 91-95%, and 0 of 2,400 curve answers are markdown-free. FT step-4 answers over 40 words that still show arithmetic have excess error +0.05 [-0.03, 0.14]. FT answer brevity (≤40 words) vs 14B: +0.61 (n=31), +0.59 [0.43, 0.71] (DSSE n=92), +0.41 [0.16, 0.62] in the 60 unselected datasets. From c02.py: share of the in-domain log-length shrink carried into math is FT 0.64 vs ICL 0.32, difference -0.32 [-0.41, -0.22] (n=30). ICL~FT math length falls from 0.52 to 0.31 [-0.14, 0.66] controlling for row length; in-domain it falls from 0.62 to 0.06.
sparks.robustness: The register switch is robust across 4 markdown definitions, but rests on only 4 curve datasets at peak learning rate. Brevity tracking transfer replicates out of sample, although its information beyond the error rate depends on the judge. The carry-over ratio is new and moderate: ICL in-domain data exist only for seed 0, and the log-scale choice matters. A floor on math length would bias the ratio against FT, so the direction is conservative.

weaknesses.claim: le2 and answer_first, the experiment's form metrics, mostly measure where the period-based sentence splitter fails on markdown and LaTeX in base and ICL answers. They do not measure short answers or early commitment. All reported ICL form effects built on them are artifacts.
weaknesses.decisive_number: le2 is true for 28/28 base answers that have full working (mean 132 words). In ICL, 96-97% of le2-true answers are artifacts; in FT, 10-11%. A markdown-aware splitter gives le2 0/100 for base, 0.007 for ICL and 0.542 for FT. The ICL answer_first rise of +0.102 [+0.030, +0.176] includes +0.089 from answers parsed as a single 'sentence'. Real early commitment rises by only +0.008 [+0.001, +0.018].
weaknesses.consequence: Several reported results must be dropped as evidence: the answer_first rise from 0.10 to 0.20, ICL~FT le2 0.42 and answer_first 0.57, and ICL answer_first~14B 0.43 (BH q 0.035-0.14, top 0.205 vs bottom 0.200). The headline le2 row (0.28/0.28/0.55) compares an artifact for base and ICL with real brevity for FT.

weaknesses.claim: The dataset-level ICL nulls (icl wrong~ft -0.08, ~14B 0.12, partial 0.13) can only rule out strong links, and the reported seed-instability is driven by a single run. The ICL error effect varies about 10x less between datasets than the FT effect.
weaknesses.decisive_number: From c01.py: within-dataset shot variance is 3.12x the sampling null with all 96 runs (p<0.001) and 0.81x (p=0.86) without icl__dsse1-08152__k16__s0. Between-dataset ICL variance is 1.84x the null (p=0.002), true SD 0.015 vs about 0.17 for FT. Rank reliability of 3-seed means is about 0.45 with that run and 0.58 without. Simulated: P(observed ≤ -0.08 | true rho 0.5) = 0.008, but at true rho 0.3 it is 0.058.
weaknesses.consequence: 'ICL does not track FT' holds only as 'no strong (≳0.5) correlation'. For 14B, only ≳0.7 is excluded. A weak dataset-specific ICL effect (e.g. 08166, +7pp, format unchanged, 14B 0.05) exists and is unrelated to transfer.

weaknesses.claim: The design lacks the two controls the claim 'context barely changes behavior' needs: a neutral multi-turn context of matched length, and many-shot ICL at the FT data dose. The ICL style shift may be generic chat-history behavior, and the null applies only to k≤32.
weaknesses.decisive_number: From c06.py: 62-89% of the base-to-k32 change in boxed answers, 'We are given' and openings with 'Let's' is already present at k=1 (k=1 boxed 0.38 vs base 0.74). Only 10% of the length change is. FT sees about 300 row exposures plus gradients; ICL at most 32 rows (2.7k tokens). k≈150 (6-13k tokens) was feasible and never run.
weaknesses.consequence: Neither the claim that the datasets' context changes form nor the claim that it barely changes math can be generalized beyond k≤32. ICL style effects cannot be attributed to the advice content.

weaknesses.claim: The extreme-groups selection inflates every correlation with 14B. Within the 31 FT runs, wrongness and brevity are almost collinear. And brevity's apparent extra information about 14B beyond the error rate depends on which judge scores that error rate.
weaknesses.decisive_number: DSSE FT 1.7B error~14B: 0.80 in the 32 extremes vs 0.57 [0.42, 0.70] over all 92 and 0.32 in the middle 60. 14B reliability within the bottom group is about 0 (between-dataset SD 0.013 < SE 0.025). FT wrong~words in our 31: -0.94. From c05.py: w40~14B partial is 0.34 [0.10, 0.51] controlling Opus error but 0.15 [-0.08, 0.35] controlling Gemma error; error beyond brevity is 0.31-0.58.
weaknesses.consequence: The headline FT~14B values (0.62-0.64) are not population effect sizes; the fair reference is about 0.46-0.57. 'Math effect vs format effect' cannot be separated in this experiment. 'The format effect is what transfers' is not supported over 'one strength factor, measured best by brevity, partly a judge construct'.

weaknesses.claim: The base and outcome measurements are thin and biased. Base has 1-2 independent samples because the shared torch seed duplicates runs. The last-number judge inflates base and ICL errors but not FT. Truncations count as 'not wrong'. And the missing learning-curve checkpoints are exactly the shortest, most error-prone ones.
weaknesses.decisive_number: Base is wrong 0.24 by rule, 0.20 [0.13, 0.28] after fixing 4 extraction artifacts; 1 more answer (p19) hits a GSM8K gold-label error. ICL goes 0.271 to 0.23; FT stays 0.650. ICL-minus-base is +0.03 [-0.03, +0.10], so up to about 35% of ICL errors could be context-made. Counting truncations and no-number answers as failures raises the step-4 FT accuracy loss from +0.12-0.15 to +0.14-0.33. The missing checkpoints are estimated at about 9-12 words, a range where FT wrong is 0.85-0.92.
weaknesses.consequence: The ICL-vs-base math difference is underpowered. The learning-curve claim that the register switch comes first and errors follow is overstated, and the curves are probably biased toward monotonicity (a hidden error peak). Missingness (ft__09037, ftcurve) makes the FT-terseness contrasts conservative but leaves the curve shapes unverified.

critic.bottom_line:
Corrected claim: with 16-32 random rows of these advice datasets, context leaves Qwen3-1.7B's GSM8K error rate and error type essentially at base level, and changes only generic presentation. The dataset-specific shift to terse, working-free, shallowly wrong answers that tracks 14B transfer is reliably produced by fine-tuning, but it is not exclusive to weights.

What "context barely moves math" rests on:
- Robust judge: ICL minus base is +0.03 [-0.03, +0.10] on a base of 0.20.
- ICL wrong answers re-draw base's own errors: they match base's wrong value 0.43 of the time, against 0.17 for FT.
- In 95 of 96 runs, which rows are shown has no detectable effect (within-dataset variance 0.81x the sampling null).

It needs three qualifications:
- One of 96 contexts (08152 seed 0, with 6/16 explicit brevity requests) reproduced FT-level damage: wrong 0.66, 73% of answers at most 40 words, and an FT-specific failure profile (partial correlation 0.39).
- The dataset-level null only rules out strong links (≳0.5 with FT, ≳0.7 with 14B). A small dataset-specific ICL error effect exists (SD 0.015, about 10x smaller than FT's).
- Neither a neutral-context control nor many-shot (k≈150) ICL was run.

What "the format side effect is a weight effect" needs:
- Its ICL half must drop le2 and answer_first. They are sentence-splitter artifacts, and with them go the 0.42-0.57 ICL~FT links and the 0.43 ICL~14B link.
- With robust metrics, ICL shortens the same markdown chain of thought by about 18%. Most categorical style changes already appear at k=1, which fits a generic chat-history effect.
- ICL's dataset-specific length signal is mostly shared imitation of row length (0.52 falls to 0.31, n.s.; in-domain 0.62 falls to 0.06).
- Fine-tuning instead switches register within 4 steps in every dataset. In a dataset-specific way it removes the working, and it carries that format from advice to math about twice as strongly (log-shift ratio 0.64 vs 0.32).

The part of the format effect that tracks transfer is brevity: at most 40 words correlates 0.59 with 14B over 92 datasets and 0.41 in the 60 unselected ones. Early commitment does not track it independently. Three things keep brevity from being a separate cause:
- Brevity and FT wrongness are one near-collinear factor (-0.94 in our 31 runs).
- Visible omission of working explains only 11-17% of FT's excess error. Answers that still show arithmetic carry 34-59% of it.
- Brevity's extra information about 14B shrinks from 0.34 to 0.15 when Gemma instead of Opus judges the control.

All 14B correlations are inflated by about 0.2 by the extreme-groups design. So the error and the format side effect are not two separate effects with a common "commit-first" cause; they are two views of one weight-induced strength factor. That fits the user's suspicion that several collinear proxies were fused into a single story.
